argument:
The bear's declining cloud gross margin is a real counterexample to stable incremental cloud economics. It does not negate the matched 18% growth in consolidated revenue and operating income: at the group level, the latest quarter maintained substantial operating profitability despite that cloud pressure. This is a different measure from gross margin, so it cannot establish cloud-unit returns, but it argues against generalising the segment pressure into group operating deterioration.

The buy scenario depends on maintaining those group economics and translating them into cash after infrastructure investment. Debt and FCF are unknown, and investment/discrete EPS gains should not carry valuation. At 29.26x vendor earnings with an extended chart, current entry requires additional support. The bear identifies incremental capacity risk while the supplied group results sustain a narrower profitability thesis.
key_points: Group operating growth matches revenue despite cloud gross-margin pressure.
Group operating margin and cloud gross margin are distinct measures.
Infrastructure-adjusted cash and normalised value remain necessary.
rebuttal_to_previous: I concede no stable marginal Azure return follows from its growth rate. But cloud gross-margin compression does not erase the observed consolidated operating-income growth of 18%, matching revenue. The group profitability thesis survives while FCF and incremental capacity returns remain unverified.
